summary: This component renders an interactive map of blog articles as a force-directed graph on a canvas, where nodes represent articles and edges show how they link or share topics. It loads pre-computed layout data from a plugin, draws meerkat stickers as nodes (falling back to colored dots when too small), handles hover and click interactions, and degrades gracefully to a plain list on mobile or without JavaScript.

explanations.59: This type defines a lookup table mapping image file paths to already-loaded HTMLImageElement objects, so we don't reload the same sticker twice.
explanations.73: These constants store the transparency (alpha) levels for different edge types — 'link' edges are darker/more opaque than 'tag' edges because links matter more visually.

explanations.92: We measure how wide the text will be when drawn, so we can calculate the bounding box of the label and check it against other labels.
explanations.99: This checks all four sides of two rectangles: if they don't overlap on ANY axis, they don't collide at all.
explanations.118: We read CSS custom properties (variables like `--ifm-color-emphasis-500`) from the document root so the canvas colors match the current theme without hardcoding hex values.
explanations.135: If the node is too small to show a readable face, or we haven't downloaded the sticker image yet, return null so the caller draws a flat colored dot instead.
explanations.150: We calculate how much to scale the image so it covers the full square area without leaving gaps — this crops instead of stretching the sticker.
explanations.157: Docusaurus plugins expose their build-time data through this hook; the blog-graph-plugin computed the nodes and edges at build time.
explanations.171: Canvas doesn't react to CSS variable changes automatically, so we bump this counter when the theme changes, which triggers the draw effect to re-read colors.
explanations.176: We start with an empty object and gradually fill it as sticker images load, so nodes can draw with or without their faces depending on what's ready.
explanations.180: We track URLs we've already tried to load (including failed ones) so we never retry a broken image on every redraw — failed assets get their colored dot and stay that way.
explanations.185: This media query listener detects when the viewport crosses our mobile breakpoint and triggers a re-render; we clean up the listener on unmount.
explanations.203: The canvas graph only shows on desktop after the component mounts (avoiding hydration mismatch); mobile and non-JS users see the plain list instead.
explanations.217: We extract the unique mainTag values from all nodes by creating a Set (which deduplicates) and spreading it back into an array.
explanations.225: We sort tags by their *displayed* label (e.g., 'Intelligence artificielle' in French) not by their key, and pass the current locale explicitly to avoid hydration mismatches.
explanations.232: This filters the full node set down to either the top N by importance (default view) or all nodes matching the selected mainTag.
explanations.242: Canvas height adapts to what's actually visible — a filtered view with 2 nodes gets a short canvas instead of inheriting the default 120-node height.
explanations.280: We convert the Set of paths to a sorted, space-separated string so React sees this as a stable dependency — switching filters back and forth won't re-download already-loaded stickers.
explanations.284: We find which sticker paths we haven't tried to load yet by checking against our requestedRef tracker.
explanations.291: This creates a promise for each missing image; the promise resolves with either the loaded Image or null (if loading failed).
explanations.300: withBaseUrl prepends the locale prefix if needed — without it, /fr/map/ would request images from /img/ instead of /fr/img/.
explanations.303: We wait for all image loads to finish, then batch-update state once so we only re-render once instead of once per image.
explanations.323: The list fallback ignores the top-N cutoff (a plain list has unlimited room) but still respects mainTag filtering so the dropdown control feels responsive.
explanations.355: We multiply by devicePixelRatio so the canvas stays sharp on high-DPI screens like Retina displays.
explanations.363: We apply the DPR scaling to the canvas context so all our drawing commands automatically scale to match the canvas's physical pixel resolution.
explanations.379: We multiply the base alpha for this edge type by an additional dimmed factor if there's a hover active but this edge isn't connected to the hovered node.
explanations.395: We check if this node is in the neighborSet (nodes one edge away from the hovered node), so we can decide whether to dim it.
explanations.431: This helper queues a node for labeling if it exists and hasn't already been queued, then calculates where its label should appear (to the right of the node).
explanations.456: After collecting all label candidates, we ask selectNonOverlappingLabels to keep only the ones that don't overlap, then draw those winners.
explanations.486: We iterate through visible nodes to find which one (if any) the mouse is over, checking if the click position is within the hit radius of the node's circle.
explanations.491: This is the distance formula: if the squared distance from the click to the node center is less than the squared hit radius, we hit that node.
explanations.512: We need withBaseUrl because history.push() doesn't auto-add the locale prefix the way the Link component does — otherwise /fr/map clicking a node would try to navigate to /blog/x instead of /fr/blog/x.
